purpose: Count pages without losing items or dividing by an invalid page size.
integers: Both inputs and the result are signed 64-bit integers. Python receives ordinary int values in that range; bool and other Python objects are outside this contract.
valid_result: For items >= 0 and size > 0, return the least nonnegative integer p such that p * size >= items. The mathematical specification uses unbounded integers.
invalid_result: Return -1 when items < 0 or size <= 0. Do not divide or calculate a remainder on those paths.
evaluation: Evaluate the invalid-input guard left to right with short circuiting. On valid inputs, evaluate the quotient, then the remainder, then the selected return. Arguments have no side effects.
overflow: The quotient is at most items. A nonzero remainder implies size >= 2 and quotient < items, so adding one is within i64. The implementation never calculates items + size - 1 or p * size in i64.
errors: The function returns the invalid-input sentinel rather than raising or panicking. There are no other errors within the declared input and resource assumptions.
generalization: Repeat both directions after renaming the function and moving its source. No repository identity or function name may select translation semantics.
scope: An independently checked bounded translation example, not a proof of arbitrary programs, complete language equivalence or a runtime benchmark. The Rust and Python implementations are authored development examples, not unfamiliar repositories.
